newsitem.title: USA: Analyst says U.S. bank stocks face tougher times.
newsitem.headline: Analyst says U.S. bank stocks face tougher times.

text.p: Lawrence Cohn, a veteran analyst who was dismissed this week by PaineWebber Group Inc, is sticking to his views that bank stocks face a more difficult environment.
"The stocks have been selling at record high valuations," he said in a telephone interview Wednesday. "I think it's going to be tough to make money in bank stocks going forward."
Since banks stocks peaked in early March, he said, they have fallen more rapidly during downturns in the overall stock market.
When the market has gone up, bank stocks have moved up less rapidly. "Sentiment is starting to shift against the group," he said.
Cohn said for the bank group "revenue growth has slowed down substantially and earnings growth is going to follow."
As for his departure from PaineWebber, Cohn said, "they fired me." He added, "all they told me was that Michael Culp wants his own team."
Culp recently joined PaineWebber as equity research director from Prudential Securities. Culp replaced Ann Knight who went to Salomon Inc's Salomon Brothers.
PaineWebber said in a press release Wednesday that Ruchi Madan, who was banking analyst at Prudential, has now joined PaineWebber.
Cohn said it was obvious that he was let go to make room for Madan.
A PaineWebber spokeswoman would only say that Cohn "left the firm."
Cohn said he is now looking for another job.
